notes: Catalysis paper on N-ethylcarbazole (EC) LOHC hydrogenation/dehydrogenation over Pt/Ni on N-doped graphitic carbon. The 'H2 storage capacity' of 3.79-5.80 wt% (Table 2, Fig. 6, 200 C, 40 bar) is hydrogen incorporated into liquid EC, computed from GC product distribution; it is a reaction, not gas-phase uptake by a sorbent, and is not counted under I1. The only I1-qualifying data are the H2 pulse physisorption/chemisorption volumes of Fig. 7 (flow method, AutoChem II) for Pt/Ni@(N)G-0 and Pt/Ni@(N)G-18; the sorbent is carbon-majority (C 71.9-73.8 wt%, Ni 14-15 wt%). Borderline calls: (1) I1 met on Fig. 7 although these are catalyst-characterisation chemisorption data; if I1 were judged not met, the code would still be no_conditions_stated. (2) I3 not met because the adsorption temperature is only 'room temperature' in words (data dictionary: a condition stated only in words is not a number and is not imputed). If a reader accepts the room-temperature statement as stating T, I3 would be met and the code would then fall to I4, no_surface_area (Ni metal area only, basis unstated). No retraction (is_retracted false), not a review, no duplicate-data statement.
